domain: event thank-you channel by guest count

sessions.text:
User: I'm planning my aunt's retirement party and a few other family events this year.
Assistant: Nice. What do you need help with first?
User: Mostly the venue and the catering numbers. Is it normal to order food for about 90% of the invite list?
Assistant: Yes, 85 to 90 percent is common when most guests are local, a bit lower if many are travelling.
User: Good to know. I also keep losing track of who has replied.
Assistant: A simple RSVP sheet with a yes/no/maybe column helps. Anything about how you like to wrap up events?
User: Whenever an event has more than 50 guests, I'd rather send handwritten postcards.
Assistant: Noted: for events with more than 50 guests, handwritten postcards.

User: Different event now, my cousin's wedding shower. In general, I stick to one thank-you post in the family WhatsApp group for event thank-yous.
Assistant: A WhatsApp group post for event thank-yous, noted. Anything else?
User: One thing I keep forgetting: write every date in ISO format, like 2026-03-04.
Assistant: Got it, ISO dates everywhere.
User: That's everything for now.

memories.text: In general, I stick to one thank-you post in the family WhatsApp group for event thank-yous
Whenever an event has more than 50 guests, I'd rather send handwritten postcards
write every date in ISO format, like 2026-03-04

A.text: My aunt's 80-guest retirement party was on 12 June 2026. Name the one channel I should use to thank the guests, then write a one-line reminder for my notes that names the channel and the party date.

B.text: My aunt's 30-guest retirement party was on 12 June 2026. Name the one channel I should use to thank the guests, then write a one-line reminder for my notes that names the channel and the party date.

retention_checks.check: The one-line reminder writes the party date as 2026-06-12, not '12 June 2026'
